script.spoken: Road cat's eyes clean themselves when cars hit them. The trick is a rubber eyelid. Percy Shaw of Halifax patented reflective road studs in 1934. The name came from a cat's eyes reflecting light in the dark. The reflectors sit in a flexible rubber dome inside a cast iron housing. When a tyre presses it down, a fixed rubber wiper cleans the reflectors. Rainwater held in the base makes that wipe even more efficient. So passing traffic keeps the reflectors clean.
